We found that this object has a critical frequency corresponding to a surface magnetic field strength of about 30 Gauss, and an orbital period that suggests an object with a mass less than 0.005 Jupiter masses. We also observed variations in the object's orbital phase and estimated a mass of about 10^-4 to 10^-3 Jupiter masses, which could be consistent with a planet orbiting the binary.

This research introduces an innovative method for generating realistic digital human movements, tailored for virtual avatars used as virtual representatives in digital human interfaces. Our approach, dubbed ANR, utilizes a simulation to establish a baseline for human movement patterns, which is then combined with a neural network-based character control system. The resulting hybrid system enables intuitive control through a combination of keypoint inputs and a physiological simulation, yielding high-quality movement patterns. Our analysis through motion capture data demonstrates that ANR produces human-like movement patterns, significantly outperforming existing systems. Additionally, we investigate the integration of learning-based keypoint estimation into our model, enabling a more direct and efficient control method. Overall, our work makes a significant contribution to digital human interfaces by providing a new, flexible, and realistic method for generating human-like movements.

This research examines the unique effects of modifying images in a way that is not immediately noticeable to humans but significantly impacts image quality, specifically focusing on harsh image modifications. The study uses a specialized deep neural network to introduce intense image modifications and evaluates their effects on human and machine perception. Human subjects and an automated method to measure network performance are compared to understand how modifications influence both natural and artificial vision. The results reveal a novel phenomenon where humans surprisingly adapt to such intense modifications, while machine vision is uniquely sensitive to them. Moreover, the study reveals that modifying images in a way that alters local contrasts significantly affects both human and machine perception, despite being largely invisible to humans. The source code for the device and image modification algorithm is available on GitHub at https://github.com/alexey-kaznello/HiViDe.

The Chern-Simons theory when coupled to a knot, when studied in the presence of degenerate representations, results in the formation of the Askey-Wilson algebra, which then acts upon the theory's state space. By calculating the resulting knot polynomials and comparing them to those resulting from standard Chern-Simons theory, we find that the two are related in a specific mathematical sense. A new method for computing link invariants in low-dimensional spaces has been developed, taking into account degenerate representations in the Chern-Simons theory's gauge group, $SU(N)$. This method not only deepens our understanding of the theory but also reveals a specific relationship between the two algebras that governs the s-invariant within its basis.

We perform a quantitative analysis of the magnetic properties of 2D structures composed of frustrated trimer subunits connected weakly, using a cluster quantization scheme to simulate the effects of magnetic fluctuations on a molecular magnetic model. Our analysis reveals that the ground state magnetic properties are influenced by both intra-trimer interactions and weak links between trimer units, leading to a phase diagram characterized by two distinct phases: antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic. Additionally, the impact of another molecular parameter on the system's magnetic behavior is examined within the established framework, and the results are correlated with existing experiments to provide an accurate representation of the system's magnetic properties.

To enhance the capabilities of zero-shot educational applications, it's crucial to fine-tune language models for specific educational purposes. Unfortunately, there's a lack of consensus on the optimal method for fine-tuning. In an effort to address this, we've carried out a comprehensive meta-tuning study, which involved simultaneously adjusting the parameters of the model and its training data. To achieve this, we've created a range of training datasets and corresponding prompt sets for each educational domain by combining and reconfiguring them in various ways. The results of our study show that, in many educational contexts, fine-tuning a zero-shot language model can yield notable improvements. Moreover, we've discovered that there's a more effective method for fine-tuning educational language models than previously thought, which we've now successfully demonstrated.

We examine three complex Higgs singlet models with non-holomorphic terms that modify the Z boson's pole mass and electroweak phase transition. A novel phase transition model in these theories surpasses the critical requirements for electro-magnetic and gravitational wave formation and avoids the issues of charge parity and charge reflection symmetry breaking problems that affect other similar models with additional scalar fields. We explore how we can identify and observe the characteristics of the resulting first-order electroweak phase transition through the analysis of LHC searches for the Higgs sector along with the properties of dark matter, as well as observations from future gravitational wave detectors such as LISA. We find that the gravitational wave signals produced by the phase transition in these singlet Z3-matter models may be detectable by LISA within a few years.

We have created an automated tool called High-z Sudoku to simulate and strategically design deep sky surveys in the millimeter and submillimeter bands. By doing so, it aims to minimize the complexity of determining redshifts from a given number of candidates in an area of space. We employed this program to compare the efficiency of various frequency combinations in achieving this goal. Our results indicate that the optimal number of frequency measurements needed for robust redshift determination ranges from 4-6 observations per source in certain redshift ranges. Furthermore, we analyzed several existing surveys and discovered that the ALMA Large Program 949 utilizes 10 different frequency bands in a manner that allows High-z Sudoku to predict robust redshifts across 90% of targeted sources spanning redshifts of 3.5-6.5, although there are a few identified cases where the predicted accuracy may be limited.

Neutron scattering experiments on a triangular lattice antiferromagnet, specifically a triacetate compound with the formula Cu$_3$(DHA)$_2$(py)$_2$(NO$_3$)$_2$, reveal a range of low-energy magnetic states. Upon cooling, the material undergoes a structural phase transition which leads to two distinct spin lattice dynamical states. The first occurs below 140 K and is characterized by increased spin fluctuations and a shift in the material's equilibrium temperature from its original Nél\'e temperature. The second phase is observed below 100 K and is marked by significant fluctuations in the material's dynamics, as well as increased temperatures from a new N\'el\'e temperature. The first phase's behavior aligns with theoretical predictions for a disordered spin system known as geometric frustration, whereas the unique features and frequency of spin fluctuations in the second phase suggest a liquid-like system state.

Our research on nonabelian gauge theories with fundamental fermions reveals a new phase when coupled to a scalar field through a minimal Yukawa interaction. In four-dimensional space, this combined theory exhibits a distinct phase transition from a gauge-deactivated phase, where the gauge coupling vanishes, to a limiting phase where the gauge coupling diverges as the scalar mass approaches zero. Utilizing the lattice regularized SU(3)-Higgs model, we measured the scalar mass in the limiting phase and investigated the region near the deactivation transition. By analyzing the behavior of the scalar in the deactivated phase, we determined the critical point where the transition occurs and investigated the universal properties of this critical point. Our results indicate that the deactivation transition in this model closely mirrors the confinement transition observed in the pure SU(3) gauge model.

Cr2Al, a compound with the tetragonal I4/mmm space group, displays antiferromagnetic properties through its in-plane arrangement and is characterized by its c-axis symmetry. Neutron diffraction studies at a temperature of 1.5K have identified two equivalent magnetic models, both involving Cr 2+ moments of 2 muB aligned along the in-plane axis. Additionally, our computational analysis has revealed the existence of specific exchange relationships, including both in-plane and out-of-plane interactions, which have been further supported by simulated neutron diffraction measurements. These interactions show significant thermal evolution in their intensity, particularly for the in-plane Cr 2+ exchange relationship.

An enhanced kinetic equation, which incorporates the collision frequency dependent on molecular velocities and applies to gas flows far from equilibrium, is proposed and examined through comparison with experimental findings. Initially, theoretical arguments are presented to establish its theoretical basis. A key advantage of this proposed model is its capacity to accurately represent collision dynamics across a wide range of interatomic potentials and rarefaction levels. Furthermore, empirical evidence gathered through direct comparisons with available experimental results show that the model accurately captures gas stream parameters not typically well-explained by the Maxwell Boltzmann collision model. Specifically, it accounts for collision process asymmetry, which is influenced by both molecular potential and Knudsen number, thereby offering a promising starting point for developing speed-dependent collision models through ab initio calculations.

A widely accepted theory suggests that humans possess an innate ability to understand language, known as naturalized interpretation. Unfortunately, most contemporary language models rely heavily on large amounts of labeled data and do not effectively naturalize their output. Unlike conventional models that learn from vast amounts of data, we have discovered that traditional approaches can be adapted to take advantage of extremely limited resources by labeling fewer, high-quality sentences and obtaining additional support from sentences manually inspected by humans. Specifically, we explored how to use annotated explanations to improve semantic interpretation performance. Notably, our study demonstrates that the combination of massive pre-training on unlabelled text and the incorporation of explanatory annotations can lead to significant improvements of up to 20% in low-resource environments. Moreover, our results suggest that models trained on explanations not only achieve better performance, but also develop more accurate and coherent understanding of underlying semantics.

The future Electron-Iон Collider will surpass the performance capabilities of conventional particle colliders due to its novel collision mechanism that incorporates both electron and ion beams. This advanced understanding of heavy-ion physics will significantly benefit the fields of QCD, heavy ion research, and the study of b-quarks and baryon-to-meson ratios. 

To effectively capture the vast amount of data anticipated, the futureEIC will require an enormous number of particle collision readings per second, necessitating an enormous amount of data to be processed simultaneously. 

Highly advanced silicon sensors, specifically those with an inner p-type layer (IPM), have been shown to have a superior response time. Studies were conducted using IPM sensors with p-n and p-i-n configurations to analyze their performance. 

Using a specialized laser source, time-resolved measurements were performed to investigate the influence of the IPM layer on the response time of the p-i-n diode. 

To further understand how the IPM layer affects charge collection, simulations were performed with the TCAD Sentaurus software. 

To verify the IPM layer's thickness, a secondary SIMS measurement was conducted. 

By comparing the simulated results with the measured data, it was found that the time-of-flight of charge was in good agreement with the simulated results, and the IPM layer's thickness was found to be in agreement with the SIMS measurement. 

Overall, the research demonstrated that the incorporation of the IPM layer significantly improves the response time of p-i

We've discovered rapid brightness fluctuations in two exceptionally bright AGNs, 2MASX J0842-5959 and 3C 279, during their observations. Fluctuations were observed in the UV band, with fluctuations repeating every few hours. The analysis showed fluctuations in both AGNs with amplitudes of about 0.7 standard deviations. Notably, 2MASX J0842-5959 exhibited fluctuations in all spectral bands, with fluctuations in the optical and near-infrared bands. The fluctuations in 2MASX J0842-5959 were in agreement with theoretical predictions based on the radius of the disk and gravitational time delay. On the other hand, 3C 279 showed fluctuations in the UV and optical bands, but not in the near-infrared band. The phase analysis showed a correlation between the light curves. Furthermore, the light curves were analyzed using the Fourier transfer technique, with the results suggesting that pulsational instability was a potential cause of fluctuations, particularly in 2MASX J0842-5959. However, alternative explanations, such as stochastic variability, were also considered.

Observing the radial magnetic field in HD58260 is challenging due to its low value.
We utilized three specific iron lines to analyze the stellar chromosphere's behavior.
The stellar spectrum was analyzed using a model accounting for temperature and abundance variations, as well as microturbulence and stellar velocity, to derive a magnetograph.
We analyzed a specific spectral region and measured a significant variation in magnetic field strength, confirming a strong correlation with previously discovered magnetic field variations.
We found that the low surface magnetic field value of HD58260 results in a non-axisymmetric structure.

A novel method is introduced for explicitly depicting one-dimensional Dunkl intertwining operators $V_{\alpha}$ in terms of free boson operators $a^\dagger$ and $a$, leveraging a system with two bosonic modes $a_1$ and $a_2$. This approach may have broad applications in the field of mathematical physics.

A young galaxy like NGC 5253, which has a relatively low metallicity, presents an ideal setting to study star formation in early universe conditions. Our analysis of a young stellar population in NGC 5253, based on ALMA's H30α line observations, reveals the distribution of recent star birth across the galaxy. By examining these data in relation to the Galaxy Evolution Experiments simulation, which replicates star formation in the galaxy, we were able to develop new metrics to measure the timing and concentration of star birth within NGC 5253. Our findings show that the majority of star birth in NGC 5253 has occurred within a 1.5 kpc radius from the galaxy's center, and that the star formation rates in NGC 5253 have varied over time. Our metrics indicate that the majority of star formation in NGC 5253 has occurred within a relatively recent time period, and that the star formation rates in NGC 5253 have been more concentrated in the galaxy's outer regions.

A countable group G qualifies as having the VC property if any equivalence relation generated by virtually infinite cyclic groups on a set D, along with any associated E-dynamical system, can be simulated by an equivalent relation generated by virtually infinite cyclic groups on a similar set D', plus a suitable random element. In the context of group actions, this definition translates to a scenario where two actions of G on different spaces, which are virtually cyclic equivalent, can also be considered conjugate, including a common, compact metric space on which both groups act in a mutually equivalent manner. This paper presents an enhanced version of the previously mentioned virtually infinite cyclic property specifically for acting on finitely presented groups and establishes the compactness theorem for virtually cyclic equivalence among such group actions.

Estimating conditional expectation functions, where the dependent variable y is influenced by explanatory variables x, is a fundamental task in econometrics. However, a major issue arises due to finite sample sizes and noise in data, which typically lead to significant estimation biases in nonparametric methods, particularly when calculating function function integrals such as mean regression functions. To address this challenge, a novel data fusion technique is introduced, combining data-driven and stochastic ordering-based methods to minimize the impact of bias while reducing the effect of noise. Furthermore, to enhance the accuracy of bias estimation, a data-driven technique is proposed, which results in significant computational efficiency improvements. The method's effectiveness, measured by lower mean squared error, is demonstrated through a large-scale simulation using a subset of the Consumer Expenditure Survey dataset.

The spread of highly contagious diseases like SARS-CoV-2 is difficult to study due to limited access to complete system information. Mathematical models are used to analyze disease dynamics but their complexity is hindered by the lack of available data. This research focuses on the spread of SARS-CoV-2, using the Seir model to analyze the disease's behavior. By applying an Euler-Lagrange method, we develop ways to analyze the entire system based on limited, measurable components, specifically confirmed cases of infection. This research also aims to analyze the difficulty of assessing the epidemic's progression using the Krasovskii method and presents simulations to demonstrate the limitations of using only certain disease components.

Recent advances in connecting temporal knowledge graphs have gained attention and researchers have proposed various approaches, including using fixed models. Despite their ability to outperform others on certain connection prediction tasks, there has been little research into how these models impact overall performance. Our study thoroughly examines the role of fixed models in temporal knowledge graph prediction, examining how their size affects the predictive ability of the most effective models. Through experimentation, we show that including multiple fixed relations can actually hinder the graph embedding methods' performance, and we reveal that these models are often overfitted, leading to lower predictive accuracy. Our findings also suggest that using a size-appropriate fixed model can yield lower prediction errors, but at the expense of reduced generalizability.

This article explores the implications of the most commonly used Kerr-lens stable resonator configurations, which are often employed in ultrafast optical experiments, considering the high peak power achievable through mode-locked operation. By investigating the phase mismatch between the K lock and K spot sizes, particularly their dependence on beam waist, our research reveals that Gires-Tournois effects can cause substantial wave-front distortion, which is shown to be mitigated through the use of a longer K-tube. Furthermore, this study also investigates the influence of beam waist on pulse duration, peak power, and the role of saturable mirror energy, as well as the effect of higher-order transverse modes in Kerr-lens stable resonators.

To train machine learning models on sensitive data, such as medical records, an alternative approach involves gathering user-assisted information from a secure environment. Users train a model on their local data and send the updated model to a central server, which then combines the model updates received from users. However, existing approaches fail to address the trade-off between training accuracy and user privacy, and the users' varying computing capabilities and device battery levels. This paper addresses these concerns by proposing a new asynchronous model. The proposed model prioritizes training accuracy for users with high computing power and device battery levels, while emphasizing user privacy for users with lower computing capabilities and device battery levels. The model balances user privacy and training accuracy in scenarios where users have varying computing capabilities and device battery levels through a multi-objective optimization problem. Furthermore, the model relaxes this problem and transforms it into a convex optimization problem, which then yields an asynchronous update rule for online learning. Through regression experiments conducted on a real Raspberry Pi, it is observed that the proposed model achieves a balance between training accuracy and user privacy, and outperforms existing approaches in user privacy and training accuracy when other users have lower computing capabilities and device battery levels.

Our ultrathin 3D photonic crystal cell incorporates a unique back reflector, the 3D gyroid photonic crystal, reflecting light in an omnidirectional manner and enabling efficient absorption of light in thin-film absorption materials with enhanced performance. By combining this innovative back reflector with a silicon layer and a silicon nitride bus waveguide, our 3D gyroid photonic crystal cell offers a highly efficient device suitable for low-light level applications and highly integrated photonic systems.

This paper aims to develop and iterate analytic functions, tetration being a key example. By creating a family of functions, we can asymptotically determine the asymptotic values of their n-th iterates. In the process, we set a criterion for selecting these functions and prove that they are abundant. Furthermore, we examine the effect of changing the selection criteria on the resulting asymptotic solutions to the tetration problem for large real numbers. Additionally, we introduce methods for improving the convergence of certain power series related to this topic, thereby enabling us to compute specific values of the function within the radius of convergence.

High dimensional expansion, also referred to as high dimensional programming, offers an alternative approach to high dimensional expansion, utilizing high dimensional covers to provide tight bounds for mixing times and spectral gaps of Markov chains. Due to its flexibility, high dimensional expansion can be applied across various problems, including hypergraph expansions, quantum data processing inequalities, and coupling bounds for Markov chains. Recently, a new high dimensional expansion structure was proposed, allowing it to achieve improvements for a range of examples and applications. In contrast, we introduce a novel framework for constructing high dimensional expansions, offering more flexibility and flexibility in choosing the dimension and number of Markov chains. Our work demonstrates that we can create efficient high dimensional expansions for hypergraph covering problems and mixings of related Markov chains. For instance, we prove the existence of high dimensional expansions for 2-regular 3-uniform hypergraphs with a fractional Benjamini-Kalei-Zahavi expansion of 12.955 using the first moment method, and we show that there exists a 2-regular 3-uniform hypergraph with a fractional Benjamini-Kalei-Zahavi expansion of 13 using the second moment method. Moreover, we provide a comprehensive study of the relationship between high dimensional expansion, coupling, and Markov chain mixing.

Within the family of 3d-4f-3d magnetic compounds, unique materials with exceptional magnetic properties can be identified. These ternary compounds, specifically perovskites and honeycomb-based compounds, possess an inverted band structure, allowing the possibility of achieving a magnetic state dominated by the transition metal, potentially giving rise to magnetic properties driven by the spin of the transition metal, as seen in antiferromagnets. This possibility is supported by theoretical calculations indicating that in honeycomb-based compounds with large, negative spin-orbit interactions, the magnetic moment contributed by the 3d electrons overcomes the suppression from the topological effect. As a result, honeycomb 3d-4f-3d compounds are promising to exhibit magnetic properties driven by the spin of the transition metal. To investigate this, a detailed study was conducted on GdInO$_{3}$, an exemplary antiferromagnet featuring a centered honeycomb lattice, where spin-orbit coupling plays a pivotal role. This study involved measuring the temperature-dependent in-plane and out-of-plane magnetization of GdInO$_{3}$ using a SQUID magnetometer, and comparing its in-plane magnetic response with that of the analogous compound, GdCuO$_{3}$. These measurements, coupled with theoretical predictions, revealed a significant spin of the 3d electrons in GdInO$_{3}$, thereby validating that three-dimensional magnetic properties can be generated through 3d electron

The challenge of link prediction in large-scale network analysis is significant, particularly when dealing with sparse graph representations. Traditional methods, focusing on node embeddings, have been found to be insufficient for predicting edges in such networks. Our research presents a new approach to sparse link forecasting using sparse spectral signal analysis and embedded manifold learning. We call this approach SSNE. First, proposed is a novel spectral signal embedding that leverages a sparse adjacency matrix as a kernel for similarity measurement and an efficient O(n^2) distance computation scheme. Then, a novel sparse-based SE, preserving the intrinsic graph structure, is developed. Our analysis shows that SSNE is not only more precise but also faster than current state-of-the-art methods. Our experiments demonstrate the ability of SSNE to predict links in synthetic datasets, such as ER graphs, and a benchmark real-world link prediction task.

The development of deep nanofabricated silicon vapor chambers with a high aspect ratio of around 50 is presented, which can be customized in length of around 1 cm and wide area of 1 x 1 cm.  The deep silicon vapor chambers are suitable for integrating with surface micromachined optical components and electronic circuits using advanced nanofabrication techniques.  The deep silicon vapor chambers are equipped with microheaters and driven by sophisticated temperature sensors to maintain precise gas pressure and temperature control.  The internal wall surface exhibits minimal contact angles with atomic vapor, ensuring uniform wall vaporization.  The wall surface's high reflectivity of around 90% is achieved through a metal coating.  The deep silicon vapor chambers' performance is evaluated in terms of atomic beam velocity and atomic density.  The atomic density is measured to be on the order of 10^13 atoms per cubic centimeter, demonstrating a 10-fold increase over conventional vapor chambers.  The atomic beam velocity is estimated to be around 300 meters per second.  The performance of the deep silicon vapor chambers is compared with that of more traditional chambers.

To mitigate the impact of nonlinear impairment in dense single-carrier transmissions, DFT-s-OFDM is commonly employed, which utilizes DFT spreading to break up the signals' nonlinear phase coupling. However, the effectiveness of DP4D-DFTs in minimizing nonlinear distortion is still underexplored. A novel model has been developed to evaluate the power of nonlinear distortion in DP4D-DFTs. By accurately matching Monte-Carlo simulations, the model achieves a close alignment of the mean nonlinear distortion power across various transmission scenarios. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that DPT4D has a more significant nonlinear distortion effect than DP. Notably, the effect of data variance on nonlinear distortion varies with the data amplitude, which contrasts with the characteristics of single polarization systems.

Wildfires pose a significant threat to life, property and the environment, making their early detection and monitoring a top priority. Recent studies have shown that integrating multiple image spectra can enhance image analysis, though existing methods rely on complex statistical models and lack flexibility. We propose the FiRe-GAN, a deep learning-based image synthesis network, inspired by recent advances in Generative Adversarial Networks, capable of generating realistic red, green, blue images from near-infrared, visible near infrared and visible far infrared images. The FiRe-GAN's four-channel design enables exploration of novel data sources and applications in visible imaging by adding a second visible channel. We evaluate the proposed method's effectiveness in fire visualization and simulation, demonstrating its ability to improve fire simulation accuracy, particularly in simulations involving the combination of near infrared and visible far infrared images.

Detecting signs of depression on the internet could help reduce misinformation about mental health and alleviate the severe consequences of a severe epidemic of untreated mental illness. However, accurately classifying posts about mental health poses significant data-related difficulties. A major issue is that publicly available datasets used for machine learning applications are often not representative of diverse demographics and can be biased towards individuals who have sought professional help. This paper aims to rectify this by introducing a more comprehensive dataset, drawn from Reddit threads featuring discussions on generalized depression and related conditions. The dataset comprises 10,000 text posts, including discussions from individuals experiencing depression and those offering support or discussing alternative conditions. To enhance the dataset's value, it is accompanied by annotations indicating discussions of depression and other mental health conditions. Furthermore, we develop and evaluate classification models utilizing various architectures, including character-based neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and transformer-based systems, as well as ensemble methods. Our study highlights the importance of diverse data representation in training robust classification models capable of accurately classifying text across various demographics and groups.

This paper delves into the characteristics of a random graph model, consisting of $n$ vertices, where each vertex is assigned to one of several compartments following the SIR model commonly used to simulate an epidemic. Edges between the vertices are deemed present with a probability that varies according to the SARS-CoV-2 transmission rate and the numbers of susceptible, infectious, and susceptible populations. As the number of vertices approaches infinity, the model is demonstrated to converge to a limiting object, revealing the emergence of a giant component. Various aspects of the model are analyzed in detail.

This study provides a comprehensive theoretical analysis of the Full Shell Model (FSD) predictions for the Isoscalar Giant Monopole Resonance (GMR) in $^{24}$Mg and $^{28}$Si, incorporating coupling effects with the Isoscalar Giant Quadrupole Resonance (GQR). Our calculations reveal a significant shift in the energy of the GMR in $^{28}$Si compared to the Harmonic Oscillator (HO) model predictions, contradicting experimental findings. In contrast, the calculated GMR energy in $^{24}$Mg aligns with experimental measurements. These discrepancies are resolved through a stochastic variational Hartree-Fock (SVHF) approach, which generates a more detailed and accurate basis compared to the traditional HO model. Our analysis indicates that in $^{28}$Si, coupling with the GQR significantly lowers the GMR energy. Notably, the stochastic variational HO transformation offers a straightforward solution to the problem of GMR description, effectively integrating the effects of the GQR without the need for complex calculations. This method is expected to be even more effective for heavier deformed nuclei.

This paper examines the stability of stick-slip systems controlled through feedback mechanisms, within a broader class of dynamical systems that encompasses well-known models such as the van der Pol oscillator and the Elman spring as special cases. Our research establishes that under feedback control, stick-slip exhibits a convergence property towards a singular, unmovable equilibrium state. To validate these findings. we performed numerical simulations of a friction-driven test-bench that demonstrated the self-excited and limit-cycle behavior of stick-slip under open-loop conditions. However, when feedback control is applied, stick-slip oscillations cease entirely and the system converges to a static equilibrium state, consistent with the theoretical results.

Reinforcement learning algorithms are susceptible to failure, particularly those based on gradient methods which can experience instability.  We introduce probabilistic policy gradient methods utilizing generalized advantage estimation to enhance stability.  Building on this framework, we explore risk-sensitive reinforcement learning as a means to improve General Safety Design by incorporating risk-aware objectives.  Specifically, we integrate the Bellman risk criteria to evaluate reward functions and identify policies that are both effective and safe.  Our approach can be applied to either of the proposed probabilistic policy gradient methods.  Initially applied to a problem involving General Safety Design, we demonstrate the efficacy and benefits of our proposed methods compared to existing alternatives.

To enhance the performance of sequential recommender systems, specifically in terms of 
next item prediction accuracy and user experience, researchers have proposed an innovative 
approach that focuses on extracting a more comprehensive representation of user intent. 
Traditional sequential recommender systems primarily consider the item sequence a user has 
initiated, but by integrating additional interaction data that is not publicly visible to them, 
this proposed approach can provide a more comprehensive understanding of user intent. 
A theoretical framework has been developed to define and analyze the relationship between 
public and private interaction sequences to reconstruct a more comprehensive user intent 
representation, thereby improving the accuracy of next item prediction and overall user 
experience recommendations.

This study proposes an extension of the standard method for solving a matrix form of a confluent Heun equation, which arises from the non-linear Schrödinger equation's 'outset' through a specific transformation. Initially, the 'outset' was transformed into a solvable matrix form by Takasaki in 2006. We now extend this technique to also solve a generalized form of the equation, which incorporates the double confluent Heun equation. By employing the standard Takasaki algorithm, this new equation can be linearized into a form of the double confluent Heun equation, allowing for the discovery of numerous solvable cases that were previously unknown, including isolated and clustered cases. Furthermore, our results highlight a previously overlooked connection between the standard and generalized equations, revealing an additional solvable case that was overlooked in the original research. In addition to these findings, we also explore the connection between the obtained linear forms and Witten type second order equations, using the dependent variable transformation proposed by Fukutani et al. in 2009, to reveal additional solvable cases that were previously unaccounted for.

The assessment of rank-one matrices is a core component of matrix completion techniques in various fields, such as collaborative filtering.  As an essential tool in these applications, much research has been conducted to improve its accuracy.  Our study, however, addresses a previously underexplored issue - the possibility of group-level variations in such matrices across different groups of users.  To investigate this further, we develop a statistical model for analyzing the group-level differences in rank-one matrices.  Our results indicate that as the number of groups tends to infinity, the estimated group parameters converge at a rate of n_g/g, where n_g is the number of observations for a particular group and g is the total number of groups.  This finding has significant implications for applications in which multiple groups are observed simultaneously.  Our research builds upon past studies by providing essential insights into user profiling within multi-group settings and highlights the need to consider group-level variations when such variations exist.

The theoretical essential topological representation was proposed and demonstrated for the Ginzburg-Landau model without any symmetry constraints, using an energy function incorporating a topological component, and its existence within the space of H^1 was proven. Moreover, for a given topological index n, the topological energy function's constant value of |$\frac{u}{|u|}$| is n, thereby ensuring that each critical point of this energy function represents an n-vortex solution, and it was shown that these solutions correspond to minima under the assumption of radial symmetry. Finally, it was argued that the proposed energy function may also be applied to other models lacking symmetry.

This study focuses on the semi-inclusive Lepton Flavour Universality (LFU) ratio $R_{E}$, which compares dilepton energy spectra from $B\to V\ell^+\ell^-$ decays, accompanied by additional decay products from the vector meson. By considering these semi-inclusive decays, the uncertainties caused by the longitudinal polarization of the vector meson are eliminated, offering an alternative method to test this process. We investigate the behavior of $R_{E}$ in various kinematic scenarios and examine its sensitivity to new physics through the calculation of next-to-leading order (NLO) contributions within an effective Hamiltonian framework. We provide numerical results and discuss how future data from the LHCb and Belle II experiments can constrain this observable, leveraging its simplicity in measurement and reduced dependence on hadronic form factors.

For robustness against component failures and ease of use, it's essential for a control system's architecture to be both modular and adaptable. A control architecture with this feature, when a new element is added, requires minimal adjustments to the controller and plant regulators. We introduce a novel approach to achieving this objective in network control systems. It involves a distributed architecture where each node independently controls a specific area of the network and when a new area is added, only the control of the node's own environment needs to be adjusted. The existing regulators for other nodes remain untouched, offering a highly reliable and scalable control system. The underlying math shows that the system's stability can be determined by the stability of individual, independent regulators, making the overall performance predictable and stable. The approach was tested on a network controlling the flow of chemicals, and its results were found to be identical to a fully centralized control system.

The COVID-19 outbreak is a major global event that has had far-reaching consequences on society, the economy, and healthcare systems worldwide. Given its complex nature, classifying COVID-19 patients into different categories based on disease severity proves to be an intricate issue. To address this challenge, researchers proposed a novel approach leveraging the BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representation from Transformers) model to identify key attributes such as clinical, epidemiological, demographic, and treatment-related information. To test the effectiveness of this approach, the authors created a two-phase categorization framework, where the first phase distinguishes between COVID-19 patients and healthy individuals, followed by a second phase subdividing COVID-19 patients into three severity levels. To evaluate its performance, the authors developed a comprehensive COVID-19 dataset comprising clinical, epidemiological, demographic, treatment, and image data. Experimental results demonstrate that their two-phase categorization framework outperforms state-of-the-art models, underscoring its significance and effectiveness.

This article examines the fundamental concepts of network analysis, including graph theory and algorithms for navigation and optimization. It explores the origins of network theory, the core properties of graphs, the application of random graphs, the measurement of networks through degree distribution, clustering, and connectivity. The article also discusses the significance of communities within a network, the dynamics of searching networks using various algorithms, and the process of linking networks together. Furthermore, network alignment and flow are key considerations, which network scientists must address when researching these complex systems. Network scientists are now venturing into the realm of simulating real-world networks, such as those based on physical properties or evolutionary processes. The article serves as a starting point for researchers in a broader field, covering the core concepts of network science. It primarily targets those familiar with basic programming and mathematical concepts, such as calculus and matrices. Network analysis is a rapidly evolving field, constantly evolving as researchers discover new insights and uncover new applications.

The intricate interplay between environmental dynamics and the adaptability of life forms is a key issue in the understanding of how ecosystems evolve and diversify. Research has shown that changes in the environment, whether they occur rapidly or slowly, can profoundly impact the rate and direction of evolutionary adaptation, and conversely, biological evolution can influence the speed and direction of environmental shifts. Identifying the factors that regulate these environmental dynamics and the mechanisms through which ecological and evolutionary processes impact one another is a significant challenge. In this study, we examine eco-evolutionary dynamics across a broad timescale using a mathematical model inspired by Lake Baikal's ecosystem, focusing on the dynamics of lake levels and the evolutionary adaptation of its endemic species. Our results demonstrate that species' life histories and physiological characteristics, such as growth rates, mortality, and the strength of selection, play a crucial role in shaping evolutionary dynamics and the potential for rapid adaptation. In contrast, abiotic factors like water inflow, precipitation, and snowpack have a considerable impact on the dynamics of lake levels, leading to complex patterns of fluctuation and stability.

Unsupervised speech representation learning has shown its potential to enhance speech processing tasks. On the other hand, research has found that after being educated on a specific task, models often experience a decline in performance on related tasks. This phenomenon is called representation collapse. In the case of speech, the causes of representation collapse remain largely unknown. Our research investigates the phenomenon of speech representation collapse by creating a framework to study it. The causes of representation collapse in speech are shown to be due to education and it occurs due to two mechanisms: a shift in the class distribution of the training data, and the minimization of reconstruction errors. The implications of these mechanisms reveal two important characteristics: first, that after being educated, hypothesis representations become more resistant to adversarial attacks, second, that although educated representations become more precise in terms of a specific measurement, the useful information within them actually diminishes.

This research aims to examine the potential of decentralised, blockchain-driven systems to embrace and improve distributed marketplaces by exploring the blockchain framework in depth. The study focuses on the key characteristics of blockchain, such as its ability to operate in a distributed, decentralised, and automated manner, coupled with its transparency and ease of use across various devices. By leveraging these features, blockchain-powered distributed systems are capable of facilitating the creation of secure, verifiable, and traceable transactions within complex supply chain networks. The study also highlights the importance of widespread adoption of such technologies to improve market efficiency, particularly in the supply chain space, where streamlined tracking systems are in high demand.

Missing data significantly hampers statistical analysis, yet exclusion of such data creates bias, whereas imputation can complicate analyses due to uncertainties in missing values. A robust statistical method, the 'e-value,' quantifies the probability of findings arising from flawed data by representing it as an 'e-type' p-value. This paper introduces a new Bayesian sensitivity analysis approach for missing data using the 'e-value,' focusing on missing covariates in logistic regression models. A simplified scenario with a single missing covariate allows examination of how varying odds ratio estimates and uncertainty change in response to different prior probabilities of correct dataset values. Furthermore, the method can be extended to incorporate prior probabilities in the form of mixtures based on available dataset subsets to evaluate the robustness of statistical findings to data quality issues.

The quantum plane $\mathbb{C}[x,y]$ over the field $\mathbb{C}(q^{-1})$ has multiple possible actions from the quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, but only one corresponds to the standard representation, excluding two specific values of $q$. By focusing on the Laurent expansion ring $\mathbb{C}(q^{-1})[q^{\pm1},z]$, we find that every possible $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-action can be classified as either the standard one, or a variation involving a additional parameter.

The ever-connected world of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has turned cars into intelligent devices, supporting applications such as smart driving assistance, autonomous systems, and vehicle maintenance services. As these vehicles become hubs for sensitive data, their potential for malicious attacks has significantly increased, posing a threat to driving safety and privacy. To address this challenge, researchers have explored the adoption of blockchain technology to protect data security and privacy through decentralized, immutable ledgers, and secure peer-to-peer communication. A comprehensive review of literature is required to assess the current research landscape and fill knowledge gaps in this area. This study provides a systematic literature survey of secure federated learning frameworks for IoV, analyzing relevant papers from 2018 to 2022 based on predefined selection criteria. It examines and categorizes survey papers that integrate blockchain and federated learning in IoV, while highlighting the need for more in-depth research in this area.

Our research focuses on the production of particles created in proton-proton collisions at a high-energy collision of 5.02 TeV. We investigate the production process of charm quarks at this energy level and analyze the creation of events containing D mesons formed from the decay of B mesons, in addition to those produced directly. We look at two types of events - those with D mesons paired with jets and those with D mesons paired with photons produced in association with a jet. We examine the production characteristics of these events as a function of the transverse momentum of the D mesons up to 40 GeV. We also investigate ratios of production and find them in line with expectations from theoretical models. Furthermore, the findings of this study are compared to simulations based on the parton-hadron-transport model and a perturbative QCD model, in addition to a global analysis model. We found that, in general, the theoretical models align with experimental data.

The burgeoning field of quantum computing has achieved growing momentum with the advent of "millikelvin platforms" tailored to experimentally validate quantum computing capabilities that outperform classical counterparts in achieving tasks that surpass classical computational capabilities. Our team at Fermilab has constructed an expansive platform featuring 14 millikelvin dilution refrigerators, incorporating Dillon Devices' computational system, incorporating a groundbreaking 4092-qubit superconducting quantum computing system. This massive platform enables the deployment of cryogenic electronics on any of our refrigerators. In this paper, we document the details of our platform and explore its potential uses in scientific research across various fields, including high-energy physics.

This research paper focuses on identifying and understanding programming errors specific to a cryptocurrency implementation using Python, a language renowned for its simplicity yet prone to misuses due to ambiguous documentation. To address this, a study was conducted on a cryptocurrency library, revealing 18 distinct misuses out of a total of 11,118 issues reported, 1,082 issues from the official GitHub page, and 1,341 issues on Stack Overflow. Notably, 85.7% of these misuses are tied to the cryptocurrency's core functionality. To enhance a developer's understanding and skill set, suggestions are provided for improving a documentation generator to automatically produce user-friendly documentation. Furthermore, a method is outlined for identifying misuses from a software's issue logs, which could be applied to the cryptocurrency's issue logs from the official GitHub page and Stack Overflow, where the results are discussed.

Tagging people in videos without the need for manual intervention is a crucial aspect of many computer vision tasks. The difficulty arises from the fact that people's attributes can change over time, and there are no clear boundaries between these changes. Furthermore, the process of tagging large datasets is both time-consuming and labor-intensive. This project aims to address these challenges by using a database created from automatic phone polls. The dataset consists of people's self-reported information, which can be used to generate attribute-based data for attributes such as age, gender, and skin color. The results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy (around 85%) in generating attributes from camera roll images. The project also explores the effects of image quality and image source on the results. The created dataset is now publicly available for use.

Seismic reflectivity, representing underground geological structures, is a critical component of traditional CMP seismic data. While conventional deep learning-based seismic reflectivity inversion methods rely on sparse assumptions, they struggle to accurately recover reflectivity in cases with non-uniform seismic noise. To address this, a new optimization model integrating the proximal mean and L1 norm assumptions is proposed, enabling sparse seismic reflectivity inversion. The model's optimization can be achieved using the proximal mean network (PMNet), a network designed to approximate the corresponding optimization operation. Furthermore, a Proximal Mean Network for Non-uniform Seismic Reflectivity Recovery (NuSPAN) is introduced by replacing the standard L2 norm in PMNet with the non-uniform seismic noise-adapting L1 norm. The efficacy of NuSPAN is demonstrated through synthetic data experiments, yielding superior results over existing methods.

We focus on the analysis of translation semigroups within a variant of the Bloch-Apostolico space, specifically within the context of one-dimensional complex plane. Crucial to this investigation are the backshift semigroups, accompanied by an in-depth exploration of the boundedness of integral operators, specifically involving kernels with singularities on the unit circle. The study also involves a comparative analysis with the L^p Apostolico space for 0 < p < 1. The findings reveal that the kernel's behavior near the unit circle is somewhat flexible in terms of its integrability near the boundary, depending on the value of p. The notion of 'K-convexity' for kernel functions is introduced and it is proven that for a kernel to produce a compact operator for 0 < p < p_c, it must be convex, while for p > p_c, non-convexity can be a factor in achieving compactness. The inclusion of quasi-convexity and convexity as options for the K-convexity property enriches the understanding of bounded and compact operators in this context. Furthermore, the characterization of the infinitesimal generator of translation semigroups and its relationship with the inclusion of operators in this study are explored.

Within the context of gauge theory, we investigate the large-N behavior of the wave function wavefunction wavefunction, denoted as $\Psi_N(t)$. A key aspect involves examining the overlap of these wave functions, leading to an effective approach for computing the free energy at low temperatures and for finite system sizes. Our analysis focuses on the Haagerup model, a non-diagonalizable matrix model that exhibits universality in its spectral statistics and stationary phase approximation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the effective method accurately reproduces the Haagerup model's free energy across various scenarios.

Historical documents present unique challenges for NLP due to outdated spelling and unidentified language types like archaic or foreign languages. ArcENERGY addresses these issues with an open-source tool capable of transcribing and labeling parts of Cypriot archival documents dating back to the 19th century. By utilizing a Supervised Interval Time Series Forecasting approach, the system depends on a robust transformer model BERT for archaic Cypriot language, which is why we developed a new specialization of BERT, called ArchibERT. Additionally, the system's reliability was assessed using three evaluation metrics for interval labeling combined with anomaly detection. Results demonstrate that ArchibERT effectively predicts part-of-speech tags for approximately 93% of the documents' 87,000 words.

We provide a concise and comprehensive framework for one key area, specifically for the L1 norm on the space of functions of a bounded variation, involving nonlinear optimization problems with a constraint that is not smooth. To address these problems, we introduce a measure of function variation that is local in nature and we also establish a measure of non-local structure for a class of functionals that are nonconvex and not lower semi-continuous. Furthermore, we extend our framework to handle problems that are non-convex and non-smooth in a broader sense. To achieve this, we examine the space of functions with a total variation that is not a measure, a space that is equivalent to it for a specific class of problems with a convex and lower semi-continuous constraint. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework, we apply it to a variety of problems, such as a non-convex and non-smooth version of a phase-field fracture model and a phase-field model for brittle fracture with a state constraint.

We introduce a pioneering system that streamlines the process of converting user requirements regarding cities into formal specification. Utilizing a knowledge graph to capture city characteristics and an NLP-powered semantic query interface, we enable non-expert users to articulate the desired city features. NLP technologies then convert user input into logical formulas and generate suitable stochastic models of city behaviors through Markov Chain generation. These models facilitate further quantitative analysis through the use of monitoring tools. Our system's capabilities are demonstrated through a range of practical case studies highlighting its significance.

As large-scale practical quantum computers approach realization, reliable error correction techniques are crucial given current quantum hardware's high error rates. Consequently, there is a need for methods to mitigate errors without the need for extensive logical qubit sets. We have developed an innovative approach to significantly reduce error rates in quantum computations. This method utilizes a classical control strategy, searching for a set of inverse circuits that effectively counteract the effects of quantum error channels. When applied to circuits comprising noisy gates and its corresponding inverse circuits, the noise impact is substantially diminished, resulting in improved accuracy. We have tested this method on superconducting quantum platforms, specifically the IBM quantum computer with 127 qubits, demonstrating its potential to enhance actual quantum computation capabilities.

We investigate the ability to depict preorders using pushouts in a general, well-handled category setting. Generally, this involves defining an equivalence relation based on a given map, applying it, and then checking for transitivity. However, in more complex categories, a direct depiction may not be feasible, so we explore alternative methods. Specifically, we introduce a new condition, equivalence connection 2-transitivity, which ensures preorder depiction through pushouts in a general setting. Furthermore, we demonstrate that equivalence connection 2-transitivity implies certain desirable properties, including density and stability under various categories operations.

Spatial extreme weather events can be represented by a two-dimensional function, such as temperature and rainfall patterns across a specific geographic area. To better understand and analyze the impact of such events on specific areas, a model has been developed to study the relationship between regional conditions and local environmental extremes. This achievement marks the first time that a multivariate spatial Gaussian copula model has been effectively applied to a real-world scenario and has significant implications for fields like agriculture, energy, and medicine where precise understanding of specific locations is crucial. To investigate the relationship between regional and local extremes in a non-parametric manner, simulations have been employed and supported by actual empirical analysis of environmental extremes in a particular British coastal location and its associated regional climate.

Inspired by human brain function, a collaborative vision and language learning framework has been developed, where a pre-trained CLIP model's visual and textual encoders are trained together with a newly designed visual-textual learning loss function. This new loss function utilizes a visual-directed text feature map to guide the extraction of descriptive features from a textual encoding. As a result, two mutually descriptive features are obtained, effectively capturing semantic information from both visual and textual perspectives. The efficacy of this approach is demonstrated through superior zero-shot VQA and image captioning performance on various benchmarks, including APER, VQA-V, and COCO.

This study introduces an operator-based method for solving matrix equations in the presence of errors. By utilizing a single operator switching technique in a unified framework, we can derive Stokes-type convergence conditions that ensure the error-boundedness of approximate matrix solutions. The efficiency of this approach is demonstrated through its application to the general linear equation and the generalized Sylvester equation. The known results for noisy matrix equations are successfully recovered using our approach, while our method also provides an framework for analyzing universally bounded solutions to noisy matrix equation systems. The proposed method is subsequently implemented in the form of an R package that is available on the Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN).

We identify the $k$-th segment of quaternionic Eilenberg-MacLane spectra through a quaternionic K-theory that applies to categories closed under idempotent complements. In doing so, we establish a connection to the periodic Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum, and we demonstrate its practical application by calculating a specific localizing system. This helps us derive the n-th homotopy group of a certain quaternionic Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum. Furthermore, we show its relevance in a "quaternionic" interpretation of a "periodicity theorem" first proven by Weiss.

We provide examples of complete local rings exhibiting compactness in various characteristics and dimensions. These examples yield the conclusion that rings meeting specific criteria - excellence, equidimensionality, F-regularity, and characteristic zero are indeed compact. Additionally, the compactness of the ring in positive characteristcs is demonstrated to be F-regular, and this compactness is characterized by the equality of two numerical invariants, H_D and H_Z.

In medical imaging, developing diagnostic and prognostic tools through machine learning and precise annotations is increasingly significant. Currently, diagnostic medicine is predominantly paper-based, and the exchange of diagnostic model outcomes is limited. Medical image analysis research is hindered by a lack of uniform standards for documenting diagnostic model results, and the field is currently limited by the exclusive use of DICOM, and the non-open-source nature of some processing tools. We propose a novel solution, Highdicom, a Python library that facilitates open-source, reproducible, and standardized representation of diagnostic model results in medical imaging, including segmentation, classification, detection, translation, and segmentation task-specific outputs aligned with input image data. Utilizing Python's PyDICOM library, Highdicom provides an easy-to-use set of tools that enable users to create compliant DICOM objects for both forward and reverse compatibility. Demonstrating its efficacy using a kidney segmentation task, our framework provides a clear framework for standardized diagnostic model result representation that can be applied across both pathology and radiology.

A detailed examination of the Noether charge associated with Einstein's equations reveals that its variation form is not uniquely representative, and an extra contribution arises from a distinct 2-form, requiring a distinct Virasoro algebra to be constructed. To address this issue, we have developed a covariant approach by incorporating a boundary term into Einstein's equations and developing a conserved current based on the Noether approach. This work demonstrates that the extra term in 2-forms can be derived from the bulk expression of the Noether current and its associated current, and this is confirmed by the development of a consistent method for computing the Schwarzschild entropy.

In recent years, the development of a common language for embedding discrete objects like words, objects, and DNA sequences has been driven by the need for better semantic representation. Our work in unsupervised embedding learning of DNA sequences is motivated by the potential for more effective and flexible DNA analysis. By using a novel method that combines sequence data and unsupervised learning, we can identify and categorize DNA sequences based on their shared characteristics, without relying on labeled data or domain-specific knowledge. The empirical results of our experiments demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms existing embedding methods, offering significant potential for the broader application of embedding learning in DNA analysis.

The interaction between metal surfaces and adsorbates results in an increase of their width. In the case of very thin films, specifically those with a thickness of 5-20 monolayers, researchers observed that the interaction between the film and substrate has a similar effect on the metal-insulator transition, specifically for the V$_2$O$_3$(0001) film and MgO(0001) substrate. By adjusting the coverage of oxygen and oxygen ions on the surface, the researchers were able to induce a significant shift in the metal-insulator transition temperature, without changing the underlying structure of the film. By analyzing changes in the film's lattice using x-ray diffraction and looking at electronic structure using x-ray photoemission spectroscopy and resonant photoemission spectroscopy, the researchers identified that the metal-insulator transition temperature change is driven by variations in the film's valence state at the surface, specifically for V $_3^+$. Moreover, the researchers proposed that the varying degrees of hybridization between the V $d$-orbitals and O $p$-orbitals at the surface, specifically for V $_3^+$, are responsible for these variations.

The Clebsch variable technique for reducing Lie-Poisson systems is an alternative approach, found to be widely applicable, unlike the de Donder-Vierney Poisson reduction method which applies to specific cases. On the one hand, nearly all instances involve the use of Clebsch variables, while de Donder-Vierney reduction relies on symmetry. This article provides a general formulation of the reduction approach and its application to the Lie-Poisson model of a rigid body.

Exoplanet research has recently gained significant interest due to the recent release of the KMTNet system and the detection of numerous new "planet-like" phenomena. Systematic KMTNet team is actively analyzing data from six prime fields and six sub-prime fields to identify and characterize under-studied, close-in exoplanets in the galactic bulge. We present a comprehensive list of 29 confirmed exoplanets from the Hong Kong University's sub-prime fields in 2018, bringing the total confirmed exoplanets by Systematic KMTNet team to 55. These planets span a mass range of approximately 1.4 to 8.0 Jupiter masses and orbital periods from 1.9 to 822.1 days. We utilize various statistical analysis methods to eliminate false positives and establish the orbital parameters and mass distributions of the detected planets. Furthermore, a simple machine learning classifier was developed to distinguish between star and planet-like signals, and the new planet samples were added to the existing mass distribution analysis of Systematic KMTNet team in 2018.

A novel algorithm has been devised to maintain the positivity of total energy and entropy in the compressible Navier-Stokes equation, a scenario in past research that was only possible for the incompressible version. We adapt the energy-entropy method originally developed by Kuzin, Padmanabhan, and Zeng to incorporate energy and entropy flux corrections for the Navier-Stokes equation. By adding an artificial viscosity, a key component in the Positive Particles Positivity Preserving (PPP) method, we are able to maintain the positivity of total entropy. Furthermore, a new pressure function is introduced to address the loss of positivity of total entropy in the model's limiting process.

Determining patient blood pressure in individuals without a home monitoring device poses significant challenges, especially in healthcare settings. To tackle this issue, research has focused on using machine learning algorithms to accurately estimate blood pressure based on photoplethysmogram (PPG) waveforms captured by non-invasive photonic lasers. PPG signals can be easily obtained from skin using a simple, low-cost, and non-invasive method, especially during routine medical checkups like taking a patient's photo or vital signs. Our research, aimed at enhancing public health outcomes through blood pressure awareness, involves collecting NPL data through a Python script, cleaning it, and extracting features. We then compare the performance of various machine learning algorithms - Random Forest, XGBoost, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine - to establish relationships between the features and blood pressure values. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to extensively evaluate multiple machine learning models and perform such analysis on blood pressure, leveraging PPG waveform data.

A simultaneous expansion of Schur, elementary, complete homogeneous, and q-rook symmetric functions is defined through a specialized Dyck trail. To these functions, an additional variable is added to produce an extended series. When q equals zero, this extended series simplifies to the well-known symmetric functions mentioned earlier. An identity relating to all of these extensions is discovered and this relationship has significant implications when q takes on any value, including implications in any characteristic.

Deep learning models, specifically convolutional neural networks, have achieved exceptional performance in image recognition. However, their ability to process the orientation of images remains a limitation. In this research, we investigate the effect of image rotation on deep neural networks and develop a novel set of orientation-constructional modules. These modules allow for the creation of rotation-invariant image classification networks, ultimately improving their performance on real-world applications.

For any irreducible finite-dimensional representation $V$ of the Hecke algebra associated to the SL$_3$ group at a fixed prime $\ell$, we've developed a novel relative trace equation for a specific, uniquely defined set of intervals within the Bruhat-Tits building of Sp(3,Qp) for a prime p dividing the determinant of V. This equation relates to a classical trace equation that arises from comparing virtual Galois representations, one from GL3 and another from a 3-dimensional symplectic representation of a local group, also related to the determinant of V. Notably, the Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt isomorphism of the Lie algebra of sl3 reveals that these intervals constitute a fundamental domain for the action of the Weyl group, and this combinatorial structure remains consistent across all prime values, a property that can be explained by curvature effects.

We apply a substantial flavor dependence model to the top quark and calculate its effective mass in a leading order LQCD manner, focusing on the up and down quarks. To achieve this, our model incorporates the hadron masses of the $\tau^-$, $\Lambda_b^-$, $\Lambda_c^+$, $B^0$, $\bar{K}^0$, $\B^*_{\tau^-\bar U}$, $\B^*_{\tau^- \bar D}$, $\Lambda_c^*_{\tau^-\bar D}$, and $\Lambda_b^*_{\tau^- \bar U}$. By utilizing the $\Lambda_c^*_{\tau^-\bar D}$ mass and additional inputs, our study examines the substantial flavor dependence of the top quark and its impact in a $\Lambda_Q^{(J)}$ system. Our calculations indicate that the top quark mass in the $\Lambda_Q^{(J)}$ system is as follows: $\Lambda_Q^{(3/2)}_{\tau_Q=0.45\,\mathrm{GeV}} = 285.8 \pm 1.9 \,\mathrm{MeV}$ for $J_Q^P = 3/2^-$, and $\Lambda_Q^{(0)}_{\tau_Q=0.45\,\mathrm{GeV}} = 239.4 \pm 1.9 \

We introduce a new concept called $\mathcal F$-consecutive edge-tinting number, denoted as $cci_G(\mathcal F)$, which has applications in edge coloring of graphs based on degree constraints within specified subsets. This type of edge tinting is particularly useful in graph coloring problems, particularly when dealing with nearly d Eulerian graphs of a given degree d. Our study focuses on determining upper bounds for $cci_G(\mathcal F)$ in such graphs, specifically for cases where G is a nearly d Eulerian graph containing degree d vertices, and we aim to derive bounds that are dependent on the minimum degree d and other parameters, such as $\mathcal F$. We also investigate the value of $cci_G(\mathcal F)$ in paths and cycles when vertices are given degree d.

This study proves a set of contractive inequalities for unit ball polynomials in several dimensions in a scaled $L^2$ space, using multi-variable harmonic analysis techniques.
The analysis reveals that the contraction inequalities remain valid for any subset of $\ell^1$ sequences under a weighted Bergman space setting, providing explicit weight constraints.
The research extends our understanding by addressing the long-standing open problem of the $R$-boundedness of projection operators for general $0 \le s < 1$ in dimensions $d \ge 2$.
For one dimension, the findings resolve an unresolved problem posed by J. Bourgain in 1994 regarding the same inequality problem.
The studies demonstrate the non-trivially optimal value for $s$ in one dimension and provide dimension-dependent bounds for higher dimensions.

A novel COVID-19 detection system utilizing low-dose CT (LDCT) images is presented in this study. The proposed system comprises two stages: first, a network with a time-distributed capsule layer is trained to distinguish between normal and abnormal CT images, and second, a graph attention neural network is employed to differentiate abnormal images into inflammation or ground-glass patterns. The proposed system was evaluated on the first version of the CheXplainCOVID dataset, with training conducted on 1000 normal and 1000 abnormal images, and testing on 2000 images. The Human performance was simulated by averaging the predictions of five radiologists. The experimental results reveal that our system performed on par with human experts while requiring minimal training data.

This research focuses on organizing and optimizing space in low Earth orbit. The problem of packing in low Earth orbit can be compared to packing items of different sizes into a limited three-dimensional space efficiently, while minimizing wasted space. The study in question reveals that in low Earth orbit, various structures are used by at least five times as often as others. The different frames in low Earth orbit are being used for a range of purposes, including the deployment of solar panels, collecting space debris, and testing new methods of navigation. The research was carried out to a certain extent by employing a computer program that simulates various packing methods in low Earth orbit. The outcome of this simulation was the identification of the structures with the highest frequency, the determination of their usage in different applications, and the analysis of their potential for improvement. The findings from this simulation were further supported by the review of the technical literature and the assessment of the space organization methods currently used in low Earth orbit. The research also provides a few suggestions for enhancing these organization methods. The space organization methods in low Earth orbit can be further improved by the deployment of novel packing methods, the use of modular and reconfigurable structures, and the application of sustainable materials. The paper concludes with the presentation of the most effective organization methods and the proposal of future research directions.

Creating unstructured meshes on CAD models is challenging due to their complex geometry. To overcome this difficulty, we utilize quadrilateral-based unstructured meshes composed of small, pre-defined prisms, called O-Elements, which extend from the surface into the domain. By converting mesh generation issues into linear optimization problems, we can efficiently solve for arrangements of interior clusters and their corresponding projections onto CAD features. This approach enables high-order, quadrilateral-based meshes to be generated in a semi-automatic manner, as well as other mesh generation challenges such as aligning with boundaries and removing distortions.

The correlation coefficient serves as a fundamental tool in exploratory data analysis, enabling researchers to gauge the degree of linear relationship between two variables. This study derives an analytical expression for computing sample moments of sample correlation coefficients following various permutations of multivariate normal data, with known population parameters. Although such formulas are computationally feasible for lower dimensional data sets, their application becomes computationally infeasible for higher dimensional data due to the combinatorial explosion of possible permutations. Consequently, this study develops a methodical approach to derive these formulas and employs mathematical induction to establish their validity for general dimensions. Furthermore, we provide numerical evidence that for high-dimensional data sets, calculating the mean and higher-order moments of sample correlation coefficients via the derived formulas is significantly more efficient than relying on Monte Carlo simulations.

The application of the S-matrix approach to scattering amplitudes in classical gravity is examined. Specifically, one-posteriori derivations of Newton's gravitational constant and the Schwarzschild metric from quantum scattering formulas are presented. Furthermore, the derivation of the flat space Kerr metric is demonstrated. The derivation of the Schwarzschild and Kerr metrics are generalized to incorporate findings from higher-order perturbations in quantum field theory. Additionally, the derivation of Hamilton's Jacobi equation for a scalar field in the Schwarzschild and Kerr metrics is presented.

We introduce a novel finite-dimensional interior localized feedback control scheme for solving the 2D and 3D unbounded black hole problems within the framework of the Navier-Stokes equations. This control mechanism is designed to asymptotically enforce uniform stability in both 2D and 3D domains across critical $L^q$-based Sobolev and Besov spaces, where $q$ varies depending on the spatial dimension. Our research also extends the existing literature by demonstrating the feasibility of controlling unbounded flow patterns through localized internal actuators, a concept initially explored in related works by Debussche, Fabrie, and Mandel (2013) and Fabrie and Mandel (2015).

LitMind Web Dictionary is an online dictionary platform that uses natural language processing to analyze the written words of Shakespearean plays, resulting in personalized definitions. The platform's dictionary has been trained on 70,000 Shakespearean scenes, enabling it to provide nuanced word descriptions. The platform's C++-based WDI class generates definitions by analyzing how words are used within their surrounding context, incorporating connotation and emotional tone. LitMind Web Dictionary can be customized for use with authors of any genre, requiring a representation of at least 10 scenes written by the target author type as input to the system. The platform's architecture is designed to provide a versatile definition generation system that can be adapted to a wide range of authors and writing styles.

Some researchers have highlighted the impact of both local and global fairness policies on linalg-based recommendation models. A notable compliance theory was proposed, which asserts that similar items should adhere to a fairness rule. Yet, this theory's focus on fairness is limited to a single aspect. A more significant concern is the fairness and stability of linalg models, which are also crucial for their practical application.
